title: Shadab Khan's Maiden Century Drags Pakistan From 154 for 9 to One-Wicket Win Over England
excerpt: Batting at No. 8, Shadab made an unbeaten 113 and shared a record 89-run tenth-wicket stand with Haris Rauf in Lahore. Pakistan reached the tri-series final; England lost their third match in a row.
body:
• Shadab Khan, batting at No. 8, scored an unbeaten 113 off 96 balls — his maiden ODI century — to take Pakistan from 154 for 9 to a one-wicket win over England in Lahore.
  • His unbroken 89-run stand with No. 11 Haris Rauf (7 not out off 19) is the highest tenth-wicket partnership in a successful ODI run chase.
  • Ben Duckett's 105 had carried England to 241 all out in 46.4 overs, with Shaheen Shah Afridi taking 4 for 46.
  • Pakistan reach the tri-series final; England, beaten for the third match running, must now beat Sri Lanka to stay alive.

Pakistan were finished. Chasing 242 at the Gaddafi Stadium, they had lost their ninth wicket in the 34th over with the score at 154 and 88 runs still needed. What followed, according to Reuters, was one of the great ODI heists: Shadab Khan counter-attacked from No. 8, Haris Rauf blocked and survived at the other end, and Pakistan crossed the line with one wicket and 17 balls to spare to book their place in the tri-series final.

Duckett Holds England Together

Put in to bat, England were 19 for 3 inside the opening overs. Shaheen Shah Afridi removed Tom Banton with his 150th ODI wicket and then Joe Root, and Jordan Cox fell to Rauf as England slipped to 52 for 4. Ben Duckett rebuilt with Sam Curran in a fifth-wicket stand of 93, reaching a composed 105 off 111 balls — his fifth ODI century, as Sky Sports recorded — before a top-edged slog sweep ended his innings. Curran made 42, Gus Atkinson finished unbeaten on 36, and England were bowled out for 241 in 46.4 overs. Afridi's 4 for 46 had kept a far bigger total out of reach.

The Chase Collapses

Pakistan's reply mirrored England's start. Fakhar Zaman and Babar Azam both fell for 10, Saim Ayub went cheaply, and at 31 for 3 the hosts were in the same hole. Saad Baig's brisk 32 off 22 balls and Salman Ali Agha's 26 briefly steadied things, but Jamie Overton (3 for 43) and the relentlessly accurate Liam Dawson dismantled the middle order. When Will Jacks dismissed the debutant Razaullah, Pakistan were 154 for 9 and, as Cricbuzz put it, the chase looked as good as done.

An 89-Run Last Stand

Shadab had arrived at 103 for 6 in the 24th over. From 19 off 28 balls he accelerated without slogging, picking off a boundary almost every over and farming the strike while Rauf faced just 19 balls for his unbeaten 7. Shadab finished with 13 fours and five sixes. The 89-run partnership is the highest ever for the tenth wicket in a successful ODI chase, and Shadab's hundred — reached off 95 balls — was his first in any format for Pakistan.

It nearly ended in farce. Given out leg-before to Atkinson with 21 still needed, Shadab reviewed; UltraEdge found an inside edge while players were already shaking hands. The handshakes were postponed. Rauf hit the winning runs in the 48th over.

What It Means

For England this was a third consecutive defeat and a second collapse in four days, after Sri Lanka chased 430 against them earlier in the series. Duckett's century and Overton's bowling were not enough to protect either a big total or a small one. England must now beat Sri Lanka in their final group match to have any chance of reaching the final. Pakistan, meanwhile, are through — carried there by a No. 8 and a No. 11 who refused to treat 154 for 9 as an ending.
